sections.text:
Type MFAC relays provide 
high speed differential protection for various items of power system plant 
including generators, reactors, bus bars, motors and the individual windings of 
power transformers the three element version type MFAC34 provides both phase and 
earth faults protection. The relay measuring element is basically an attracted 
armature unit of simple and robust construction, supplied from a bridge 
rectifier. setting are determined by a series of resistors, selected on a seven 
way plug bridge. type MFAC relays are suitable for use with 0.5A,1A and 5A 
current transformers at 50Hz or 60Hz .

This procedure details 
the steps required to completely check the proper operation and calibration of 
the MFAC34 relay. It is recommended this procedure be carried out on a yearly 
bases.

The document is 
formatted the way to minimize the possibility of error causing personal injury 
or damage to equipment.

Power Station, 
and certified by eng. Mona 
Ahmed Al Sharqawy: WDEPC consultant engineer 'A' and MPIS coordinator.

sections.text:
Voltage 
Pick-Up and Droop Out Check Test

items:
Connect the external power supply (220 V, 50 HZ) to the voltage injection 
 tester at terminals # 1,3 or 1,4 and the tester output terminals #1,2 will be 
 connected to the relay.
Reduce the setting to 225V

Slowly increase the voltage until the relay is picked up . The relay must 
 operate with a voltage between +/- 10% of the setting value.
Record this value on the test sheet.
Slowly decrease the voltage until the relay dropped out .
Record this value on the test sheet.
Repeat these steps for phase B and phase C.

Request the operator to switch on the main circuit 
 breaker.

Operate the output auxiliary contact by injection to 
 trip the circuit breaker.
Check that the circuit breaker tripped

sections.text: Return the Relay and Power Equipment to Service

items:
Verify the test result match the relay setting. If 
 not consult technical services.

Test trip the circuit breaker associated with the 
 relay.

Make a final check that all switches on the relay 
 are set according to the setting sheet.

Make sure the CT secondary circuit is in normal 
 condition

Remove the CT shorts which were installed in the 
 Power Supply
Return the relay and power equipment to service.

Introduction
Type MFAC relays provide 
high speed differential protection for various items of power system plant 
including generators, reactors, bus bars, motors and the individual windings of 
power transformers the three element version type MFAC34 provides both phase and 
earth faults protection. The relay measuring element is basically an attracted 
armature unit of simple and robust construction, supplied from a bridge 
rectifier. setting are determined by a series of resistors, selected on a seven 
way plug bridge. type MFAC relays are suitable for use with 0.5A,1A and 5A 
current transformers at 50Hz or 60Hz .
This procedure details 
the steps required to completely check the proper operation and calibration of 
the MFAC34 relay. It is recommended this procedure be carried out on a yearly 
bases.
The document is

A work permit must be issued

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required.
Personal safety and healthy equipment must be used as safety shoes, safety 
 helmet ... etc
Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the relay current 
 circuits for test current injection.
Switch off the DC power supply before inserting or withdrawing the relay
Outage arrangement must be done.

 before isolating the relay current circuits for test.

Testing Procedure (s)
Voltage 
Pick-Up and Droop Out Check Test
Connect the external power supply (220 V, 50 HZ) to the voltage injection 
 tester at terminals # 1,3 or 1,4 and the tester output terminals #1,2 will be 
 connected to the relay.
Reduce the setting to 225V
Slowly increase the voltage until the relay is picked up . The relay must 
 operate with a voltage between +/- 10% of the setting value.
Record this value on the test sheet.
Slowly decrease the voltage until the relay dropped out .
Record this value on the test sheet.
Repeat these steps for phase B and phase C.
Trip Test
Request the operator to switch on the main circuit 
 breaker.
Operate the output auxiliary contact by injection to 
 trip the circuit breaker.
Check that the circuit breaker tripped
Return the Relay and Power Equipment to Service
Verify the test result match the relay setting. If 
 not consult technical services.
Test trip the circuit breaker associated with the 
 relay.
Make a final check that all switches on the relay 
 are set according to the setting sheet.
Make sure the CT secondary circuit is in normal 
 condition
Remove the CT shorts which were installed in the 
 Power Supply
Return the relay and power equipment to service.
